subject: sentences
title: Parts of a book
about: The parts of a book and what each one is for: title, author, illustrator, front and back cover, table of contents, glossary, headings, bold words, captions and page numbers, plus who is telling or talking in a story. NC RI.1.5 (use text features to find facts), RI.1.6 (facts from pictures versus from words) and RL.1.6 (who is telling the story).
tip: Open any real book with him and have him point to each part as it comes up: cover, title, author, contents, a heading, a caption.

cards.q: Who writes the words in a book?
cards.note: The author writes the words. The illustrator draws the pictures.

cards.q: Who draws the pictures in a book?
cards.note: The illustrator draws the pictures. In some books one person does both jobs.

cards.q: What do we call the name of a book?
cards.note: The title is the name of the book. It is on the front cover.

cards.q: Which part of a book shows the title and the author on the outside?
cards.note: The front cover is the outside of the book. It shows the title, the author and often a picture.

cards.q: You want to find the page where the part about frogs starts. Where do you look?
cards.note: The table of contents is at the front. It lists each part and the page it starts on.

cards.q: You read the word habitat and do not know it. Which part of the book tells what it means?
cards.note: The glossary is at the back. It tells what the hard words in the book mean.

cards.q: What do we call the big words at the top of a page that tell what that part is about?
cards.note: A heading is like a little title for one part of the book.

cards.q: What do we call the words under a picture that tell what the picture shows?
cards.note: A caption is the little bit of writing next to a picture.

cards.q: Some words in a fact book are printed in dark, thick letters. What are they called?
cards.note: Bold words are important words. They are often explained in the glossary.

cards.q: What does the number at the bottom of a page tell you?
cards.note: Page numbers help you find a page from the table of contents.

cards.q: What does the back cover of a book often tell you?
cards.note: The back cover often has a few sentences about the book.

cards.q: A bird book has a picture of a nest with three blue eggs. Where did you learn the eggs are blue?
cards.note: Pictures give information too. The color came from the picture.

cards.q: The words say: A bee has six legs. Where did you learn how many legs a bee has?
cards.note: This fact came from the words, not from a picture.

cards.q: "I love my new red boots," said Mia. Who is talking?
cards.note: Said Mia tells us who is talking. The marks around the words show someone is speaking.

cards.q: The story says: I am a cat. I nap all day. Who is telling the story?
cards.note: When the story says I, the one talking is the cat. The cat is telling the story.

cards.q: "The water is cold!" said Ava. "No, it is warm," said Ben. Who said the water is warm?
cards.note: Two people are talking. Said Ben comes right after the words about warm water.
